## Statement and modeled scope

Cañete, Miranda Jr., and Vittone study the plane whose density is one on the closed strip $|y|\le 1$ and $\lambda>1$ outside it. Their existence, symmetrization, and candidate classification reduce the unresolved type-(iv) question to the possible optimality of a symmetric four-arc profile; see Proposition 3.6, Lemma 3.8, Proposition 3.9, Conjecture 3.12, Theorem 3.16, and Remark 3.17 of [@CaneteMirandaVittone2010]. The present result concerns only the formalized regular model.

Write $$f_\lambda(x,y)=\begin{cases}1,&|y|\le1,\\\lambda,&|y|>1,\end{cases}\qquad \lambda>1.$$ Weighted area is integration of $f_\lambda$ over a measurable carrier, and weighted perimeter is integration over the complete topological frontier with one-dimensional Euclidean Hausdorff measure. These definitions are [@lean:StripDensity] [@lean:WeightedArea] [@lean:FrontierMeasure] [@lean:WeightedPerimeter] [@lean:FinitePerimeterRegion].

If $\lambda\ge51/50$, every modeled four-arc candidate with $0<h\le1$, $0<\alpha<\pi/2$, density jump $1<\lambda$, and Snell law $\lambda\cos\alpha=h$ is not a weighted-perimeter minimizer among all admissible equal-area competitors. The minimizer predicate quantifies over every competitor, so one strict equal-area improvement suffices. The hypotheses and semantics are [@lean:FourArcCandidate] [@lean:FourArcCandidate.SatisfiesCMVTypeIVHypotheses] [@lean:FourArcCandidate.IsWeightedPerimeterMinimizer]. The published root is [@lean:CMVPublishedCutoff51_50.candidate_not_isWeightedPerimeterMinimizer_from_51_50].

## Geometric realization

The four-arc candidate is assembled from a strip core and two reflected exterior circular caps. The incidence law gives $\alpha=\arccos(h/\lambda)$, and the coordinate construction yields its weighted area and perimeter formulas: [@lean:FourArcCandidate.alpha_eq_arccos] [@lean:FourArcCandidate.candidate_area_formula] [@lean:FourArcCandidate.candidate_perimeter_formula].

For $0<h_3<1$, the type-(iii) carrier contains the closed strip core, two strip-side arcs, an interface segment, and one exterior cap. Its branch selection includes major, semicircular, and minor arcs. Measurability, complete-frontier realization, and the component formulas are [@lean:TypeThreeAssembly.hasModeledCompetitor] [@lean:TypeThreeAssembly.weightedArea_formula] [@lean:TypeThreeAssembly.weightedPerimeter_formula] [@lean:TypeThreeAssembly.euclidean_frontier]. The scalar formulas are not themselves competitors: the coordinate bridge identifies them with genuine carriers and transfers equal-area strict perimeter improvement through [@lean:CMVSuffixModel.TypeThreeAssembly.scalarWeightedArea_eq_typeThreeArea] [@lean:CMVSuffixModel.TypeThreeAssembly.scalarWeightedPerimeter_eq_typeThreePerimeter] [@lean:CMVSuffixModel.FourArcCandidate.not_isWeightedPerimeterMinimizer_of_analytic_typeThree].

## The interval $[51/50,9/7]$

On this interval the analytic envelope selects, for every $0<h_4\le1$, a regular $h_3$ with equal weighted area and strictly smaller weighted perimeter. The stationary fold, descending equal-area root, continuity, and sign transport culminate in [@lean:LeanSuffixAnalytic.allCurvature_typeThreeImprovement_of_envelope].

The numerical work is proof-producing exact-rational interval arithmetic. The 1,135 cells establish domain bounds, opposite-face signs, root uniqueness, negative fold signs, negative perimeter gaps, and seam coverage. Their compositions are [@lean:MiddleFaceCells.candidate_not_isWeightedPerimeterMinimizer_from_51_50] [@lean:CompactCells1003To1023.boxes0To1023_candidate_not_isWeightedPerimeterMinimizer] [@lean:CompactCellAssembly.Conditions.candidate_not_isWeightedPerimeterMinimizer]. The regular curvature argument and the endpoint $h_4=1$ are separated explicitly in [@lean:CMVSuffixModel.FourArcCandidate.weightedArea_eq_typeFourArea] [@lean:CMVSuffixModel.FourArcCandidate.weightedPerimeter_eq_typeFourPerimeter] [@lean:CMVSuffixModel.FourArcCandidate.not_isWeightedPerimeterMinimizer_of_stationaryEqualAreaPair].

## The high-density replacement

For $\lambda>9/7$, replace the two exterior caps by one upper cap of twice the old Euclidean area and expose the lower interface chord. The retained core is unchanged, so area is preserved. The complete-frontier calculation gives $$P_{\rm new}-P_{\rm old}=L\bigl(1-\lambda g(A/L^2)\bigr),$$ and the certified arc inequality makes this negative for $\lambda\ge3145460221/2500000000$. The construction and improvement are [@lean:FourArcCandidate.replacement_cap_area] [@lean:FourArcCandidate.cap_replacement_preserves_area] [@lean:FourArcCandidate.cap_replacement_perimeter_difference] [@lean:FourArcCandidate.cap_replacement_strictly_improves]. Instantiating minimality gives [@lean:cmv_type_four_not_minimizing]. Since the threshold is below $9/7$, the exact case split proves the published root [@lean:CMVPublishedCutoff51_50.candidate_not_isWeightedPerimeterMinimizer_from_51_50].

## Limit of the certificate and remaining scope

The number $51/50$ is the limit of this published certificate argument: the retained exact-rational tiling begins there, and no certificate here covers $1<\lambda<51/50$. Extending it requires new proof-producing root, branch, and perimeter-gap estimates on that interval.

Before the full CMV conjecture can be published, the existence, regularity, symmetrization, and global candidate-classification arguments must be connected to the formal model. The measure-theoretic bridge must relate reduced-boundary perimeter to complete-frontier coordinate semantics, including interfaces, joins, null sets, and all admissible competitors. Source-coordinate normalization and compatibility must also be proved without adding hidden regularity or stationarity assumptions. These are remaining closure tasks, not consequences of this cutoff.

## Bibliography

Cañete, A., Miranda Jr., M., and Vittone, D. “Some Isoperimetric Problems in Planes with Density.” *The Journal of Geometric Analysis* 20 (2010), 243–290.
supplement_introduction:
The supplement records the formal inventory behind the conventional proof. Non-generated declarations are listed exactly once; geometric definitions, analytic envelope results, carrier bridges, cap replacement, candidate exclusion, and the published root are classified as main, while lower-level measure, topology, interval-checker, and repetitive certificate infrastructure is classified as supplement. Each entry distinguishes its mathematical contract from source metadata. The two generated families are summarized separately because their leaves repeat one certificate schema.

The notation follows the main proof: $\lambda$ is the exterior density, $h_4$ and $h_3$ are type-(iv) and type-(iii) curvatures, and `WeightedArea` and `WeightedPerimeter` are the coordinate integrals from `CMVGeometry.lean`. Generated compact cells provide rational slabs and signs for the scalar suffix; generated middle-face cells provide the slanted four-dimensional transition bricks. Their representatives identify records in the common schemas, not substitutes for the aggregate composition theorems. Compilation checks proof terms; semantic interpretation remains the model-and-source analysis in the main proof.

classifications.informal_statement: For every real r, the map s maps to r exp(i s/r) is continuous on the real line.

classifications.informal_statement: For r nonzero and arbitrary real s,t, the difference of radius-scaled circle points factors into a rotated exponential difference.

classifications.informal_statement: If r > 0 and 0 < theta < pi, u_r is injective on the closed signed-arclength interval [-r theta,r theta].

classifications.informal_statement: For r > 0 and arbitrary real a,b, the Hausdorff length of u_r([a,b]) is at most max(b-a,0).
